business_scope.primary_industry_name: Corporate Scope 1-3 Carbon Footprint Auditing and Offset Brokerage

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Convention between France and the United States for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion on Taxes on Income and Capital (1994 as amended)
France–China Agreement on the Reciprocal Encouragement and Protection of Investment (1984)
EU–Canada Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA, provisional application since 2017)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier), arts. L.561-1 through L.561-50 and R.561-1 et seq.; Ordinance No. 2016-1635 of 1 December 2016 and Decree No. 2016-1636 of 1 December 2016 on the beneficial-owner register; Code de commerce arts. L.123-1 et seq. and R.123-163; Directive (EU) 2015/849 as amended by Directive (EU) 2018/843.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport of each ultimate beneficial owner and proposed legal representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary, public authority of the country of origin, or French consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation and, where applicable, certificate of good standing of any non-resident corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry or competent corporate authority in the shareholder's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of association and board resolutions of non-resident corporate shareholders authorizing the French SAS incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate legal representative or notary in the shareholder's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Sworn French translation of all non-French corporate and identity documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Underlying documents must bear a Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization before translation; translation itself is not apostilled

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney (pouvoir) authorizing the incorporation agent to sign registration formalities
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Signatory or notary in the country of execution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization when executed outside France

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: AML/KYC questionnaire and source-of-funds declaration for all UBOs
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Founder/UBO and compliance department of the incorporation agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: No external authentication; retained as internal compliance evidence

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, officers, and authorized signatories against the European Commission consolidated financial sanctions list, UN Security Council sanctions, and sanctions imposed by the French Treasury (Direction Générale du Trésor), together with OFAC SDN and sectoral sanctions lists where USD settlement, US correspondent banking, or US nexus is involved. PEP screening is mandatory before client acceptance, on any UBO or signatory change, and on at least an annual basis; enhanced due diligence requires documented source of wealth and source of funds for any identified PEP. France's FIU, Tracfin, receives all AML/CFT reports and may request the UBO declaration from the RCS/INPI registry.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet Unique des Formalités d'Entreprises operated by INPI — https://formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr, supported by the Registre National du Commerce et des Sociétés (RNCS) and Infogreffe company data
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: French is mandatory for all statutory instruments and official filings. The company name must be entered in Latin script in the RCS; non-Latin names must be transliterated into a French-compatible Latin form. The corporate legal form 'Société par Actions Simplifiée' or the suffix 'SAS' must accompany the name. Foreign-language words are permitted only if they are not deceptive and do not imply an undertaking subject to ministerial or regulatory approval. The registrar may require a French descriptive or explanatory component when the proposed name is otherwise unintelligible in French.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: crédit (where implying a regulated credit institution)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the proposed name is refused by the RNCS/INPI registrar, the applicant may file a recours gracieux with the same registrar within thirty days of the refusal. If rejected or ignored for two months, the applicant may submit a recours hiérarchique to the Minister of Economy and Finance, followed by a judicial action before the tribunal judiciaire or competent cour d'appel in the jurisdiction of the intended registered office. In urgent cases, the applicant may petition the presiding judge (juge des référés) for provisional relief. The thirty-day name reservation is not extendable; after expiry the applicant must re-file or file a modified name.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditionally permitted for a low-risk ESG carbon advisory and audit SAS. A French SAS may use a licensed domiciliation company or a managed business centre as its registered office, provided the arrangement reflects genuine commercial substance and the company maintains actual operational documents in France. A purely fictitious letterbox address, without effective management, personnel, accounting records, or physical availability for inspection, is unlawful and may result in recharacterization by the tax and commercial authorities. Because the business is a professional service activity without a statutory license, a clearly documented virtual-office arrangement is acceptable at incorporation stage.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low to moderate; approximate annual likelihood for this low-risk service entity is 5–10% absent indicators of fictitious domiciliation, tax fraud, or inconsistent ESG/carbon brokerage activity. The likelihood increases materially where the company files claims for French innovation grants, carbon offset tax advantages, or has unusually large wholesale wire turnover relative to its declared substance.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal due-diligence memorandum and AML/CFT initial file covering UBO identification, sanctions/PEP screening, and pre-incorporation risk assessment
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market rate for professional fixed-fee incorporation due diligence

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name availability search, RNCS/INPI token review, and preliminary RCS clearance
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory RNCS search and electronic filing tariffs plus professional service fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting of SAS articles of association (statuts constitution), governance clauses, and share-capital formalities
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market fixed fee for a single-shareholder or multi-shareholder SAS

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO declaration (déclaration de bénéficiaires effectifs) and filing with the RCS through the Greffe
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Greffe du tribunal de commerce and INPI/Guichet Unique
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory registry fee plus compliance counsel fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Mandatory publication of the incorporation notice in a Journal d'Annonces Légales (JAL) in the department of the registered office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory advertising tariff per line of publication

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS registration formalities and issuance of the Kbis extract
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Greffe du tribunal de commerce / INPI
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory court registry fee for business-entity registration

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille and/or consular legalization bundle, together with sworn French translation of foreign shareholder and UBO documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: French consulate or competent foreign authority, plus sworn translator
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Consular or apostille tariff plus prevailing translator fee schedule

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered-office domiciliation service through a licensed business-centre provider for the first year
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Domiciliation company or managed office provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing annual market benchmark for commercial domiciliation services

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code, Articles L.227-1 to L.227-20 and R.227-1 et seq. governing the Société par Actions Simplifiée; Articles L.123-1 et seq. governing registration and the Registre National des Entreprises; Articles L.210-2 and R.210-3 et seq. governing corporate formation and filings.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre National des Entreprises maintained by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI), with commercial registration processed through the competent local commercial court registry (greffe du tribunal de commerce).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Electronic application for registration through the Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises, including the signed SAS articles of association, beneficial-owner declaration, and supporting formation documents.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum share capital applies to an SAS. For cash contributions, at least 50% of each subscribed cash contribution must be paid upon incorporation; the balance must be paid within five years of registration. Contributions in kind are generally fully contributed at incorporation, subject to applicable auditor and valuation rules. No statutory escrow account is required, but paid-in cash must be deposited with an authorized bank or notary before registration and released after evidence of incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: First Board Resolution of [Company Name] SAS: The Board acknowledges the valid incorporation of the Company under French law and approves the subscription by each shareholder for the number and class of shares stated in the articles of association. The Board adopts [French registered office address] as the registered office and authorizes completion of all registry, tax, banking, and beneficial-ownership filings. [Name] is appointed President for the term and powers specified in the articles. [Name] is appointed, if applicable, as General Manager. The officers are authorized to execute all documents necessary to commence operations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Confirm Corporate Structure and Regulated Activity Boundaries
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI) Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises; applicable professional and financial regulators where the proposed services exceed ordinary ESG consultancy.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm the SAS form, shareholder identity, beneficial owners, registered office, corporate purpose, share capital, President, and any General Manager. Ensure the corporate purpose describes ESG advisory, carbon accounting, emissions measurement, and commercial brokerage without representing the company as a statutory auditor or regulated financial intermediary unless separately authorized.
required_dossiers: Foreign corporate documents, if applicable, with certified French translations and legalization or apostille where required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Amend the corporate purpose or governance documents if the registry identifies an ambiguity, regulated activity, or inconsistency. Obtain a written regulatory classification where the proposed carbon or offset activity may fall within financial, audit, or environmental regulation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare and Execute Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company founders and, where used, a French avocat, notaire, or professional corporate-services provider.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the articles in French, specifying the name, form, duration, registered office, share capital, share classes, transfer restrictions, decision rules, President's powers, and fiscal year. Execute the articles electronically or with wet signatures. Notarization is not generally required for ordinary SAS incorporation, except where a contribution or transaction legally requires a notarial deed.
required_dossiers: Shareholder power of attorney, if applicable
Evidence of authority for corporate shareholders
Certified translations and apostilles or legalization for foreign documents where required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct signature defects, missing powers of attorney, translation deficiencies, or statutory omissions and re-execute the affected documents before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit and Release Subscribed Cash Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorized French bank, payment institution permitted to receive corporate capital, or French notary.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary capital-deposit account, submit the executed articles and subscriber information, transfer the required paid-in cash, and obtain the certificate of deposit of funds. Include the deposit certificate in the incorporation filing. After registration, provide the Kbis extract and registration evidence to obtain release of the funds into the operational account.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to bank know-your-customer queries, provide source-of-funds evidence, correct subscriber information, or use a qualified notary or alternative authorized institution if the bank declines the deposit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A journal habilité à publier des annonces légales in the department of the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the mandatory incorporation notice containing the company name, legal form, share capital, registered office, corporate purpose summary, duration, President details, and registration details where available. Obtain the attestation de parution and retain the published notice for the electronic filing.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Request a corrected notice or republication if the legal form, name, capital, address, officer, or purpose is inaccurate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises operated by INPI, with onward processing by the competent greffe du tribunal de commerce and entry in the RNE and RCS.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Create the electronic filing, select SAS incorporation, upload the prescribed documents, complete the beneficial-owner declaration, pay the applicable charges, and electronically sign the filing. Monitor the filing dashboard and preserve the filing receipt, application number, and all uploaded documents.
required_dossiers: Power of attorney, if filed by an agent
Declaration of non-conviction and parentage for relevant individual officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Answer registry queries through the INPI portal within the stated deadline, upload corrected or missing documents, pay any additional charge, and resubmit the affected filing elements. If rejected, obtain the written reason and file a corrected application or pursue the applicable registry appeal or court procedure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Registration Evidence and Activate the Company
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI, RNE, competent greffe du tribunal de commerce, tax administration, and the company's bank.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Download the SIREN and SIRET identifiers, Kbis extract where issued, RNE registration evidence, and beneficial-owner filing confirmation. Provide the registration evidence to the bank for release of capital, activate the operational account, register for applicable VAT and payroll obligations, and maintain statutory accounting and corporate records.
required_dossiers: Kbis extract or equivalent registration evidence
VAT and payroll registration information, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct post-registration discrepancies with INPI, the greffe, the tax administration, or the bank. Submit amendments for changes to the registered office, officers, articles, beneficial owners, or principal activity within the applicable statutory deadlines.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No industrial licensing board is ordinarily applicable to office-based ESG advisory, carbon accounting, or non-physical brokerage activities. For any physical installation or regulated environmental activity, the relevant authority is the Préfet of the department, acting through the Direction régionale de l'environnement, de l'aménagement et du logement (DREAL), under the Code de l'environnement.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No general manufacturing or industrial operating permit is required for the stated advisory activity. A separate authorization, registration, or declaration under the Installations Classées pour la Protection de l'Environnement (ICPE) regime may be required if the company later operates qualifying storage, combustion, waste, chemical, or industrial facilities.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry for Ecological Transition; competent regional environmental authority and, where applicable, the Conseil général de l'environnement et du développement durable environmental authority.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt for ordinary office-based ESG consultancy and carbon accounting with no physical installation, construction project, industrial process, waste treatment, or material environmental discharge. A project-specific screening or full environmental assessment may apply if physical facilities or listed projects are introduced.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No sector-specific wastewater or VOC discharge authorization applies to ordinary office operations beyond municipal sewer, waste, occupational-health, and general environmental rules. Any industrial wastewater, air emissions, hazardous materials, refrigerants, or regulated waste must comply with the applicable ICPE permit or declaration, discharge limits, waste traceability, storage, and certified-handler requirements.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No manufacturing-specific civil-defense or workplace operating clearance is required for a standard office. The premises must satisfy applicable French fire-safety, emergency-access, electrical, accessibility, and occupational-health requirements. An établissement recevant du public may require approval by the local safety commission; leased offices should have compliant fire systems, evacuation procedures, workplace risk assessment, and structural-load verification where the building owner or use change requires it.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) under the Ministry of Economy, Finance and Industrial and Digital Sovereignty; official portals: https://www.impots.gouv.fr (professional taxpayer portal) and https://portail-public-facturation.fr (mandated e-invoicing and e-reporting public portal); customs and export-control functions are executed by Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (DGDDI) through the DELTA customs clearance system.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1 - Assess establishment: a foreign entity either (i) incorporates a French SAS through the Guichet Unique (INPI), obtaining SIREN/SIRET from INSEE and triggering assignment by the DGFiP of a French VAT registration number (format FR + key + 9 digits) and a corporate income tax (IS) file, or (ii) operates without a French permanent establishment. Step 2 - Where no French PE exists, the foreign supplier must register for French VAT before the first taxable transaction in France: EU-established entities file Cerfa form 3519-SD; non-EU entities file Cerfa form 3520-SD and must appoint an accredited tax representative (Article 289 A CGI) who is jointly and severally liable for VAT. Step 3 - The completed registration request is submitted at the competent SIE (Service des Impôts des Entreprises) through the impots.gouv.fr professional portal. Step 4 - Upon validation, the DGFiP issues the French VAT number, opens the IS file, and enrols the entity for the mandatory e-invoicing and e-reporting regime (PPF/PDP). Standard turnaround is 2 to 6 weeks after receipt of a complete dossier.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation - A French SAS is a separate taxable legal person and is not a pass-through vehicle by default; it is subject to corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés) on French-source and allocable profits, standard rate 25%, with a reduced 15% rate on the first EUR 42,500 of annual profit for qualifying SMEs with turnover not exceeding EUR 10 million. The SAS falls within the territorial scope of French taxation for its French activities, is a distinct VAT taxable person, and does not benefit from any tax-exempt zone status.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: France does not apply a US-style check-the-box election, but the following statutory elections are available to an SAS: (1) the option for transparent partnership taxation under Article 239 bis AA of the Code Général des Impôts (CGI), available for up to five consecutive fiscal years to a small unlisted SAS (up to 50 employees and annual turnover or balance-sheet total not exceeding EUR 10 million) upon unanimous shareholder consent and notification to the DGFiP; (2) the fiscal-integration election ('intégration fiscale') under Article 223 A CGI allowing a French parent holding at least 95% of the SAS to consolidate its taxable results; (3) the VAT-grouping election ('assujetti unique') under Article 267 bis CGI allowing related French entities to be treated as a single taxable person for VAT; and (4) hybrid-mismatch and transfer-pricing notification elections implemented under ATAD (Article 212 bis B CGI).

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée - TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Non-established foreign suppliers have no exemption threshold: registration is compulsory from the first taxable B2B transaction in France. For French-established small enterprises, the 'franchise en base de TVA' exemption applies up to annual taxable turnover of EUR 91,900 for supplies of goods (tolerance EUR 101,000) or EUR 36,800 for services and liberal activities, such as ISIC 7020 ESG carbon audit and advisory services (tolerance EUR 39,100); crossing the tolerance triggers VAT liability and compulsory registration. For EU established suppliers of B2C e-commerce distance sales, the EUR 10,000 pan-Union OSS threshold applies, above which French VAT is chargeable unless the OSS scheme is used.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France operates a continuous transaction control (CTC) model via mandatory structured e-invoicing and e-reporting, without a digital fiscal stamping or prior real-time clearance mechanism. Under the Finance Act 2022, as postponed by the Finance Act 2024: from 1 September 2026 all companies must be able to receive structured electronic invoices, and large enterprises and mid-caps (ETI) must issue e-invoices and transmit e-reporting; from 1 September 2027 all small and medium-sized enterprises must issue e-invoices and transmit e-reporting for B2C and cross-border flows. Mandated formats: Factur-X (hybrid PDF/XML), Peppol BIS 3.0 or UBL, conforming to the EN 16931 semantic standard. Invoices and transaction data are submitted via a certified PDP (plateforme de dématérialisation partenaire) or through the DGFiP-operated Portail Public de Facturation (PPF), which provides the national interoperability directory and API-based data transmission; no separate digital stamp is required.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to (1) exports of goods physically dispatched or transported outside the European Union by the seller or by a third party acting on the seller's behalf, under Article 262-I-1° CGI; (2) intra-Community supplies of goods to a customer holding a valid EU VAT identification number, under Article 262 ter CGI; and (3) supplies of services treated as taking place outside France under Articles 259 and 259 A CGI when the B2B customer is established outside France, which covers cross-border ESG carbon auditing, Scope 1-3 carbon footprint verification, and offset brokerage services supplied to non-French clients. The seller must retain full documentary proof of physical export or of the offshore place-of-supply rule within the statutory records period, and for intra-EU goods the customer's VAT number must be validated via VIES.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DAU - Déclaration Administrativo-Union) processed and validated through the DGDDI DELTA export clearance system
Commercial Invoice issued to the foreign buyer or offshore client
Bill of Lading (connaissement maritime), Air Waybill (lettre de transport aérien) or CMR road consignment note evidencing physical dispatch outside the EU or intra-Community movement
VIES validation certificate of the EU customer's VAT number for intra-Community zero-rated supplies
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank statement evidencing effective cross-border payment of the export proceeds
Customs export proof report extracted from the DELTA system and available via the DGDDI 'Infocentre' portal
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The DGFiP and the DGDDI jointly cross-check DELTA export declarations with VAT returns (CA3 and annex 3310-A) supporting export zero-rating and refund claims. Missing, incomplete or false export evidence leads to reassessment of French VAT at the 20% standard rate, the statutory monthly late-payment interest (intérêt de retard), and an additional penalty of 40% for intentional deficiencies under Article 1729 CGI, rising to 80% for fraudulent manoeuvres or abuse of law; refunded VAT credits are subject to retrospective clawback (répétition de l'indu) within the ordinary 3-year assessment period, extended to 10 years in cases of fraud or undisclosed activity under Article L 169 of the Livre des Procédures Fiscales. Directors of an SAS participating in fictitious export flows or sham carbon-offset brokerage additionally face criminal tax-fraud exposure under Article 1741 CGI, with a fine of up to EUR 500,000 and five years' imprisonment, plus possible disqualification and debarment from the PPF e-invoicing system.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France operates under a fully liberalized foreign exchange regime within the Eurozone. Both capital and current accounts are convertible without prior authorization. Profit remittances to non-resident shareholders are permitted subject only to standard corporate governance documentation, beneficial ownership verification, and anti-money laundering compliance. Primary hurdles include source-of-funds attestation and alignment with French tax residency rules.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Service exports such as carbon footprint auditing and ESG advisory do not trigger mandatory surrender of proceeds under French law. Repatriation is recommended within 90 days via banking channels but is not statutorily mandated. Any goods-related offset brokerage components require surrender to a designated bank account within 15 days per customs regulations.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasible through licensed EMI providers authorized by the ACPR under PSD2/PSD3 frameworks, such as specialized fintech platforms offering cross-border e-money issuance. Legal constraints include mandatory registration, capital adequacy requirements, and full compliance with EU payment services directives and anti-money laundering obligations.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote digital onboarding is permitted for French SAS entities using qualified electronic signatures and video KYC interviews. Physical presence is required only for accounts above defined thresholds or in enhanced due diligence scenarios.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transactions linked to high-risk jurisdictions or politically exposed persons
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Enhanced due diligence package including source of wealth statements, beneficial ownership register extracts, and independent third-party verification reports

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained fund origins or large unexplained deposits
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank statements, tax filings, audit confirmations, and source-of-funds declarations

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound wires via SWIFT MT103 to French IBAN accounts using purpose code 'CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION' or 'EQUITY INJECTION'. Verification requires matching client KYC documentation, source of funds attestation, and beneficial ownership proof. Correspondent banking channels used for non-Eurozone origins with full traceability.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing via SWIFT MT103 for service payments or Commercial Letters of Credit for any trade components. Settlements processed through French banking rails with complete audit trails and regulatory reporting.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: RCS annual renewal — confirmation annuelle de l'inscription au registre du commerce et des sociétés
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce via the Guichet Unique des Entreprises / INFOGREFFE portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after the anniversary of the RCS registration date each year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: After formal notice, a 10% late penalty plus 0.40% monthly interest accrues; failure to renew for successive periods may lead to administrative strike-off (radiation d'office) ordered by the Commercial Court.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual shareholder approval of statutory financial statements (approbation des comptes sociaux at the assemblee generale ordinaire)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal corporate records — registre des décisions; no government filing in ordinary circumstances
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after each financial year-end (calendar-year SAS: by 30 June), extendable only by court order
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The SAS President faces a fine of up to EUR 9,000 (EUR 45,000 for a legal-person officer) and civil damages if accounts are not submitted for shareholder approval; repeated breach may support a petition for judicial dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory annual accounts filing — balance sheet, income statement and annexes (comptes annuels), including auditors' report where compulsory
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce via the Guichet Unique des Entreprises (INPI)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month of shareholder approval and in any case no later than 7 months after the financial year-end (calendar-year SAS: ordinary deadline by 31 July)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file after formal notice carries a fine of up to EUR 1,500 for an individual and EUR 3,500 for a legal-entity officer; persistent default may trigger judicial strike-off proceedings and loss of simplified confidential-filing options.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return — déclaration de résultats CERFA 2065 series with annexes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFIP) — electronic filing on the French professional tax portal (EFI)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Calendar-year SAS: file by 15 May of the following year under e-filing rules; non-calendar-year entities follow DGFIP schedule aligned to year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a 5% surcharge on the assessed tax plus 0.20% monthly interest; after formal notice, a 10% majoration applies and DGFIP may proceed with taxation d'office.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual declaration confirming the register of beneficial owners (déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs — DBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce via the Guichet Unique / INFOGREFFE
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At least once every calendar year, generally filed with the annual accounts deposit; within 60 days after any change in beneficial owners holding 25% or more of shares or voting rights
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fine up to EUR 7,500 for a natural person and EUR 37,500 for a legal entity; the court may also impose a trading ban for up to 5 years in serious cases.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual local business contribution — Cotisation Foncière des Entreprises (CFE) declaration and settlement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGFIP as collector for the municipality or inter-municipal authority (EPCI)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Tax notice issued by 15 November; balance due by 15 December unless monthly direct-debit instalments were elected
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unpaid CFE by 15 December attracts an automatic 10% penalty plus 0.40% per month; enforced recovery may follow through avis à tiers détenteur or administrative seizure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual dividend and distribution reporting (IFU n°2427 / CERFA 2561) where the SAS distributes dividends
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGFIP with a copy to each shareholder-beneficiary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: File by 15 February (electronic filing) of the year following the calendar year of the dividend payment; paper filing by 15 March
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Omitted or inaccurate information attracts a fine of up to EUR 150 per statement and may trigger adjustment of tax credits claimed by recipients.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes) is compulsory for an SAS meeting at least two of the following three tests at the balance-sheet date for two consecutive financial years: total assets exceeding EUR 4,000,000; net turnover exceeding EUR 8,000,000; average workforce exceeding 50 employees. Mandatory audit also arises where the SAS controls or is controlled by an entity subject to statutory audit, or where shareholders representing at least 10% of capital request an audit before the annual meeting.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP — ANC Regulation 2014-03 (Plan Comptable Général) governs the SAS single-entity annual accounts (balance sheet, income statement and annex notes). IFRS is required only for consolidated accounts of certain listed groups and is not the reporting framework for a standalone French SAS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Articles R.561-20 to R.561-23 of the French Monetary and Financial Code, the SAS must file with the commercial registry at least once each calendar year a declaration of beneficial owners (DBE) confirming the list is unchanged, or an updated list reflecting transfers resulting in direct or indirect control of 25% or more of shares or voting rights, within 60 days of the change. The annual confirmation is filed jointly with the annual accounts deposit or, where that deposit is deferred, with the RCS annual renewal.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Registre des mouvements de titres — register of every share transfer, pledge and ownership movement (Register of Members)
Registre des décisions et procès-verbaux — minutes book containing shareholder resolutions and the annual accounts approval minutes (Minute Book)
Registre de présence et pouvoirs — attendance and proxy sheets kept for each annual and extraordinary general meeting

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 350 – 1,950 per year (EUR 320 – 1,800) depending on domiciliation package, mail handling and legal notification services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,100 – 5,400 per year (EUR 1,900 – 5,000) for a small-to-mid-size Paris-based SAS; higher if consolidated or extended ESG-assurance procedures are contracted

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced corporate income tax rate of 15% on the first EUR 38,120 of taxable profit for qualifying SMEs (annual turnover < EUR 10 million, 75% directly or indirectly held by individuals). Research Tax Credit (CIR) equivalent to 30% of eligible R&D expenses up to EUR 100 million. Innovation Tax Credit (CII) equivalent to 20% of certain innovation expenses for SMEs up to EUR 400,000. No general tax holiday applies; tax loss carryforward is unlimited in time but subject to an annual offset cap of EUR 1 million plus 50% of taxable income above EUR 1 million.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form n° 2065 (Cerfa n° 15946) with annexes 2065-B, 2065-C, 2065-SD; mandatory electronic filing through the impots.gouv.fr portfolio or via EDI partner software (E-TéléTVA / EDI).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual return accompanied by four quarterly corporate income tax instalment payments (acomptes).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For fiscal years ending on 31 December, the return is due by 3 May (or the second business day after 1 May if 3 May is non-working) of the following calendar year. For other fiscal year-ends, the return is due within three months of the close of the fiscal year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company identification: SIREN number, APE/NAF activity code and address.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident company operating through a French permanent establishment (PE) must state the PE's French SIREN and French APE code, e.g., 7020Z for management consultancy and carbon audit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Résultat fiscal: taxable profit or deficit before loss carryforward, computed under French tax rules from statutory accounts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only French-source profit effectively attributable to the French PE, calculated from separate PE accounts by reference to the OECD profit attribution principles.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Déficits reportables: tax losses carried forward from prior years and deducted from current-year taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The French PE may offset losses previously recognised in France, provided the same activity and continuity requirements are met; losses of the foreign head office are not deductible in France.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Contribution sociale sur les bénéfices (applicable historically) and additional 3% contribution on distributed profits (Article 235 ter ZCA CGI).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident entities are required to complete this box only when profit is distributed to non-residents in a taxable form or where specific contribution rules apply.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: 10% of the tax due if the return is filed late; increased to 40% if filed within 30 days after a formal notice and 80% thereafter. Late payment interest (intérêts de retard) accrues at 0.20% per month on the unpaid balance. Directors may additionally face a personal fine for persistent non-compliance.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Statutory dividend withholding tax rate: 30% for non-resident corporate shareholders; 12.8% for non-resident individual shareholders. A 0% rate applies under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive where an EU parent company holds at least 10% of the French entity's share capital for a minimum of 24 consecutive months.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke double tax agreement (DTA) relief, the beneficial owner must obtain a certificate of tax residence (TRC) from the foreign tax authority and submit it, together with the applicable form (form 5001 for withholding tax refund, form 5000 for advance ruling, or online claim via impots.gouv.fr), to the French tax office competent for the paying entity. The claim must be filed before 31 December of the second calendar year following the distribution, unless a treaty provides otherwise. For EU directive relief, provide a statement of qualifying shareholding held continuously for at least 24 months.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding tax on royalties paid to non-residents: 30% (Article 182 B CGI). Statutory withholding tax on interest paid to non-residents: 30% generally, except interest on commercial bank loans contracted abroad is exempt under Article 131 quater CGI. Treaty rates typically range from 0% to 10% for interest and 0% to 10% for royalties, subject to the OECD Multilateral Instrument (MLI) Principal Purpose Test and minimum substance requirements.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 400,000,000 (annual turnover or total assets) triggers the mandatory preparation and filing of French transfer pricing documentation (Master File and Local File). Country-by-Country reporting applies to groups with consolidated revenue of at least EUR 750,000,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not maintain standalone Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) of the form applied in offshore centres. Instead, the General Anti-Abuse Rule (Article L64 of the French Book of Tax Procedures), the abuse-of-law doctrine, and the OECD Principal Purpose Test (via the MLI) require genuine economic substance, local decision-making, contractual relevance and operational staff. For ESG carbon accounting or offset brokerage, the entity must evidence real premises, employees, and commercial activity in France to support treaty eligibility and deductibility of intra-group charges.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentional concealment or under-declaration of taxable profits, false accounting, or unreported brokerage commissions from carbon credit sales; use of overseas shell accounts without disclosure.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fine up to EUR 500,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years; aggravated or organised commission increases penalties to EUR 3,000,000 and 7 years. For legal persons, the fine is multiplied up to five-fold and additional sanctions include judicial supervision or dissolution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors or statutory officers who knowingly participate in or authorise evasion are jointly liable for the tax underpaid plus penalties and interest. Criminal conviction triggers personal asset seizure, travel bans, prohibition from managing a business, and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Artificial Shell Company / Abuse of Law (Abus de droit)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Establishing a French SAS without real commercial substance, transferring intangible rights or profits through a conduit entity in a no-tax jurisdiction, or structuring a transaction solely to avoid French dividends withholding or corporate income tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment with a penalty of 80% of the reassessed amount under the abuse-of-law procedure, plus late-payment interest of 0.20% per month. If the scheme invokes treaty benefits, the DTA relief is denied and fraud penalties may apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who are deemed the decisive authors of the artificial arrangement may be held personally liable for the additional assessments and monetary penalties; criminal sanctions for tax evasion can include imprisonment and travel bans.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to register as a non-financial designated business or profession, deficient customer due diligence (KYC/CDD), or failure to file Suspicious Transaction Reports (STR) with TRACFIN in relation to high-value carbon allowance or offset brokerage, even on a low-risk AML tier.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalties of up to EUR 500,000 or 10% of annual turnover for eligible entities imposed by the ACPR or the Commission Nationale des Sanctions; criminal penalties for money laundering include fines up to EUR 500,000 for individuals and confiscation of proceeds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face personal criminal liability where non-reporting is intentional or negligent and laundered transactions flow through the entity. Consequences include custodial sentences up to 5 years, fines, asset forfeiture, and travel prohibitions.
